.fallowrc.json:
Clone detection skips the crypto test harnesses: each
packages/crypto/test/checks/<section>.ts is a per-spec-section harness kept
independently readable against its CRYPTO_SPEC section, and deduplicating
them would change packages/crypto, which needs crypto human review
(CLAUDE.md). It also skips the theme files `astryx theme build` generates
from apps/web/theme/maruhi.ts (maruhi.css and maruhi.js, both marked
@generated): nobody edits them, so a repeat there is not code to share.
ignoredClones lists clone groups reviewed and kept, by the key fallow
reports; a change to either copy, or a third copy, gives a new key that
is reported again. fallow says nothing about a key that matches no
clone, so a change that removes a kept clone removes its key and note:
- dup:a3d0632d:2, dup:54dc2654:2, dup:015e31c1:2, dup:fd94bdcb:2 are
apps/server/src/do/do-mirror.ts and do-snapshot-restore.ts carrying
parallel copies of the same chain bindings: the JSON field readers,
the stagedChainAnchors folds (the membership ops, the checkpoint
tuples) and the checkpoint-row equality pass. The mirror applies
them inside the trailer's transaction over its staging tables and
refuses with MirrorPageRefused; the restore applies the subset its
pre-promotion point supports, over the restore reader's staging and
its own anchors shape, and refuses with RestoreRefusedError.
Sharing them would couple the restore reader to the mirror's
staging vocabulary for four small, stable folds; each copy changes
only when its own pipeline's binding changes.
- dup:40b1c298:2 is the staged-row iteration preamble
verifyStagedCheckpoints and verifyStagedManifests open with, and
dup:7b9fce37:2 is the live-row preservation loop verifyStagedWraps
and verifyStagedAttestations share. In both pairs the repeated
lines are the setup only: the refusal logic that follows diverges
per table (the manifest counting predicate, the wrap epoch
admission, the attestation removal exemptions), so one shared loop
would need a switch for each check it feeds.
The duplication baseline (fallow-baselines/dupes.json) holds only real
debt and is shrink-only (scripts/check-dupes-baseline.mjs, CI 5b).
fallow reports a clone group at warn, which fails neither `fallow
audit` (CI 5) nor the whole-project run (`fallow:baselines` in
package.json: CI 5a and `bun run check`). threshold fails both on any
clone group the baseline does not list instead: it is the most
duplication allowed, as a share of the scanned lines in percent, and
the smallest clone fallow reports (two copies of 5 lines, minLines'
default) is 0.0066% of today's 151,000 lines. 0.0001 stays below one
such clone until the project passes ten million lines. fallow prints
the failure as "Duplication (0.0%) exceeds threshold (0.0%)", both
values rounded. fallow's default ignores leave spec files
(`**/*.test.*`) out of clone detection, and so out of this gate.
`bun run fallow:baseline` saves the baseline with `--threshold 0`:
under the threshold the save would exit 1 on a clone and stop the
chain before the shrink-only restore

Header's entryId prop is the scaffold's documented forward-compat
hook for the version switcher (see the comment in Header.astro);
BaseLayout and DocsLayout pass it through. Kept so the owned
scaffold tracks upstream, so the unused prop warns instead of failing

Out of analysis scope: agent skills (vendored content), the deepsec
isolated workspace, the test-vector reference generation/verification
tools (throwaway; never imported by product code), and scripts/ —
standalone repo tooling run via bun, never imported.
apps/web/public holds statically served assets outside the SPA (e.g.
pages.css referenced by invite.html — AUTH_SPEC §15-3); they sit off the
module graph and would be falsely flagged unreachable.
For apps/site (Nimbus on Astro), astro.config.ts is the entry read by
the Astro CLI; src/content (MDX) plus public/ static assets are off
the module graph (src/pages routes are analyzed — fallow detects
Astro routes and layouts as entry points itself).
.astro/ is Astro's generated types/cache directory (gitignored)

Rules new in fallow 3.34 that default to warn, promoted so they gate.
The Effect dead-code rules run in every dead-code pass. The audit
diff-risk rules read only the diff against the base, so main never has
findings; a deliberate change acknowledges one with a reasoned line
above it, e.g. `// fallow-ignore-next-line added-suppression -- <why>`
before a new suppression comment

TabsTrigger / TabsContent are the Tabs component's documented
manual-composition API (Tabs.astro carries the manual-mode
detection for them) and LayerCardContent is LayerCard's content
companion; no current page composes them by hand. Kept so the
owned scaffold tracks upstream, so the unused files warn instead
of failing

The MDX registry (src/components.ts) lists Render, and Render passes
the registry to a partial's Content so partials can use every MDX
global, Render included (nested partials). The two-file cycle is the
scaffold's designed rendering loop and resolves at render time, so
it warns instead of failing

The Nimbus scaffold's UI (apps/site/src): the desktop and mobile
variants of the header nav, breadcrumbs and sidebar render the
same link lists inside different wrappers by design, and the
scaffold is regenerated from upstream (@cloudflare/create-nimbus-docs),
so hand-deduplicating its markup would only diverge from the next
regeneration. Site code outside src/ (scripts/, test/) stays gated

The data plane's barrel cycle: data.package/index.ts re-exports
verify-meta.ts, verify-meta.ts calls quotas.ts's
metaVersionsExceeded, and quotas.ts consumes the package's
DataStore / rejectData through the index. The mutual dependency
predates the package (quotas.ts already imported the data modules
directly); the barrel only makes it a file-level cycle. Every
cross-reference resolves at call time — the index has no top-level
side effects and neither side evaluates the other at module init —
so it warns instead of failing

The scoped overrides in package.json are security pins, not leftovers:
they lift exact-pinned copies to patched releases so `bun audit` stays
clean. undici 7.29.1 becomes 7.30.1 in every miniflare copy (the one
wrangler and @cloudflare/vitest-plugin share, and the ones nested under
cf and @cloudflare/runtime-types) and in @scalar/json-magic; zod 4.6.5
(@cloudflare/config, @cloudflare/vitest-plugin) and 4.1.11
(@vercel/cli-config) become 4.6.6. fflate 0.7.3 becomes 0.7.5 in satori,
which pins it exactly (GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98; @shuding/opentype.js's
^0.7.3 copy reaches 0.7.5 by a normal bun update, so it needs no
override). fallow reports them as unused because
it cannot see the transitive resolution; bun.lock shows each in effect.
Each holds its copy at that exact version, so remove an override and its
entry here once a dependency update brings the dependent's own pin to
the patched version or later.
apps/site/theme/tokens.ts is generated by scripts/build-theme.ts from
the Astryx brand theme (@generated, do not edit): it dumps the full
brand token set as a data module, and consumers import only the tokens
they use (the e2e takes accent / background today)

Tools referenced only from CLI / lint config are never imported, so they
are excluded from unused-dependency checks
(@stylexjs/unplugin and @stylexjs/eslint-plugin are referenced indirectly
via @astryxdesign/build / the oxlint config in vite.config.ts;
@effect/tsgo supplies the effecttsgo oxlint preset that vite.config.ts
imports and the patched tsrs its CLI runs the root `lint` and
`typecheck` scripts through).
pagefind (apps/site) is the same class: the Nimbus integration runs
the pagefind binary after the build to index the site; it is never
imported from site code

packages/core/test/audit-payloads.test.t:
The per-event audit payloads (audit-payloads.ts — AUDIT_SPEC §3). The
type-level half is enforced by `tsc --noEmit` (the typecheck step of the
quality gate): each `@ts-expect-error` line below must stay a compile
error, so a change that lets a key AUDIT_SPEC does not list — a provider
identity above all (§1-2) — into an audit payload fails the gate (an unused
`@ts-expect-error` is itself an error). The runtime half pins the stores'
check, which holds the same shape against a value that escaped the types
(a widened object, an assertion).
packages/core/test/identity.test.ts:
The UserId / ProviderUserId brands (identity.ts). The type-level half is
enforced by `tsc --noEmit` (the typecheck step of the quality gate): each
`@ts-expect-error` line below must stay a compile error, so a change that
lets a provider identity into an internal-user-id position fails the gate
(an unused `@ts-expect-error` is itself an error). The runtime half pins
that the brands are type-only: decoding mints without changing the value.
The KeyFingerprintHex brand (crypto chain-types.ts; mints in core
identity.ts). The type-level half is enforced by `tsc --noEmit` (the
typecheck step of the quality gate): each `@ts-expect-error` line below
must stay a compile error, so a change that lets a plain string — a
provider identity, a user id, a row id — into a fingerprint position of a
chain entry or an audit row fails the gate (an unused `@ts-expect-error` is
itself an error). The runtime half pins the mints: the format check at the
string mints, and agreement with crypto's computation at the computed ones.
scripts/check-english-pr.mjs:
English-only PR text check (ADR-0019 decision 5). Fails when the PR title,
the PR description, or any commit message in the PR contains CJK text.
PR_TITLE, PR_BODY, BASE_SHA, HEAD_SHA come from the pull_request event
(.github/workflows/english-pr.yml). Run locally with only BASE_SHA /
HEAD_SHA set to check the commit messages of a branch.
A line containing `english-exempt` is skipped, as in check-english.mjs.
scripts/check-english.mjs:
English-only source check (ADR-0019). Scans text for CJK characters and
fails if any are found outside the exemptions.
bun scripts/check-english.mjs          lines added vs the PR base ref
bun scripts/check-english.mjs --all    every tracked file (post-migration)
Changed mode is a ratchet: only lines a diff *adds* are checked, so a PR
that touches a file with pre-existing Japanese is not forced to translate
it (ADR-0019 decision 4). --all checks whole files and is for the
post-migration steady state.
A line containing the word `english-exempt` is skipped (inline opt-out for
intentional non-English data). Whole files are exempted by listing them in
scripts/english-exemptions.txt (exact path, or a directory prefix ending
in `/`).
